description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

key_constraints: Memory intensity due to tensor dimensions

selected_model_families.rationale: Established for visual feature extraction; allows for aggressive downsampling to handle high-resolution inputs and can be adapted for reconstruction or self-supervised contrastive tasks.
Patch-based processing is naturally suited to large images, as it decomposes the wide aspect ratio into manageable units; however, requires careful tuning for the small dataset size.

uncertainty_notes: Task type is highly uncertain due to missing 'target' field in the profiler report; search space assumes an encoder-backbone optimization strategy.
The dataset name 'DENTEX' suggests dental X-rays, which often require high-resolution local features (segmentation/detection), but without targets, we cannot define task-specific heads.
Optimal aspect ratio handling (e.g., padding vs. interpolation vs. rectangular patches) is undetermined.
handoff_notes: Search space focuses on the encoder/backbone only; a decoder or task-specific head must be appended if targets are identified.
Input preprocessing must handle the 1316x2850 resolution carefully to avoid OOM errors; consider aggressive stride or large patch sizes.
The evaluation metric for NAS must be a proxy (e.g., reconstruction loss or self-supervised loss) unless supervised labels are provided in a later stage.
